question.text: What will be the Paraguay River level at Asunción on December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the river level of the Paraguay River at Asunción [station](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/nivel-rio/vermas.php?id=2000086218), in meters, for December 1, 2026.
question.fine_print:
If there is no entry for that specific date at the resolution source, the value for the latest date displayed before then will be used for resolution. 

In case of inaccesibility of the resolution source, this question may also resolve according to  [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

## Paraguay River at Asunción: research brief for the December 1, 2026 level

**Summary:** On 2026-11-05 the official station read **2.45 m**. That is already only 0.25 m above the question's lower bound of 2.2 m. The river has been falling since its 3.02 m peak on 2026-10-26. The October rise came from heavy rain, starting from about 0.4 to 0.7 m. A high Paraná River downstream is probably slowing the fall by backing water up the Paraguay, but that is my inference and no source states it.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: The DMH station page for Asunción shows 2.45 m (down 5 cm). It is updated daily. [DMH](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/nivel-rio/vermas.php?id=2000086218)
- Recent daily series from the same page (m):
  - Nov 4: 2.50
  - Nov 3: 2.57
  - Nov 2: 2.57
  - Nov 1: 2.66
  - Oct 31: 2.76
  - Oct 30: 2.86
  - Oct 29: 2.93
  - Oct 26 (peak): 3.02
  - Oct 20: 2.77
  - Oct 14: 2.29
  - Oct 12: 1.81
  - Oct 10: 1.19
  - Oct 7: 0.73
- Over the last 7 days (Oct 29 to Nov 5) the river fell 48 cm, about 7 cm/day. The daily drops are getting smaller: -10, -10, -9, 0, -7, -5 cm.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The river is falling. If it kept falling at about 5 cm/day for 26 days, it would be below 2.2 m well before Dec 1. Whether the fall slows, stops or reverses depends on rain and on the Paraná backwater.
- 2026-11-05, other stations from the DMH table:
  - Upstream, all falling slowly: Concepción 1.96 m (-2), Vallemí 2.43 m (-3), Bahía Negra 2.92 m (-2), Ladario (Brazil) 0.90 m (-2).
  - Downstream: Villeta 3.04 (-5), Humaitá 6.10 (-5), Pilar 6.38 (-2).
  - Paraná River: rising at Encarnación 10.16 m (+16), Ayolas +10, Cerrito +7. [DMH stations](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/nivel-rio/indexconvencional.php)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Heavy storms hit southern Paraguay. Encarnación got 102.5 mm in one day, and alerts were issued for Itapúa and Misiones. [Primera Edición](https://www.primeraedicion.com.ar/nota/101157645/tormentas-en-paraguay-encarnacion-registro-mas-de-100-milimetros-de-lluvia-y-persiste-el-alerta/)
- 2026-11-02: The river fell 9 cm to 2.57 m. Most measuring points had been falling for about a week. DMH said the rain so far was not enough to stop the fall. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/clima/2026/11/02/el-rio-paraguay-baja-otros-nueve-centimetros-en-la-bahia-de-asuncion/), [Crónica](https://www.cronica.com.py/2026/11/02/el-rio-paraguay-sigue-bajando-y-ya-esta-en-257-metros-en-asuncion/)
- 2026-10-19: The river was at 2.74 m (alert level is 4.50 m). The city declared an emergency in riverside areas, with about 3,300 families at risk if the river reached 3.5 m. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2026/10/19/el-rio-paraguay-casi-llega-a-los-tres-metros-en-la-bahia-de-asuncion/), [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.py/pais/2026/10/16/asuncion-se-prepara-para-una-crecida-del-rio-que-podria-afectar-a-3300-familias/)
- 2026-10-12: Intense rain caused rises of up to 81 cm in one day on the lower Paraguay (Asunción +26 cm). The Paraná was over its banks at Ciudad del Este and Ayolas. [Hoy](https://www.hoy.com.py/nacionales/2026/10/12/el-rio-paraguay-tambien-se-dispara-registran-crecidas-de-hasta-81-centimetros-en-un-dia)
- Late Sep 2026: The river was about 0.43 m. [search summary of ABC/Crónica](https://www.cronica.com.py/2026/10/15/el-rio-paraguay-subio-un-metro-en-una-semana-y-preparan-refugios-en-asuncion/)

### 4. Base rates and seasonality
- September to November is normally the low-water season. The usual rise comes later, from about December onward. [ABC 2021](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2021/09/17/el-rio-paraguay-sigue-bajando-y-esta-cerca-de-superar-el-minimo-historico/)
- Comparable past years. I could not get full Nov 5 to Dec 1 series for each year:
  - 2025: 0.80 m on Nov 16 (+5 cm). [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2025/11/16/asi-estan-los-niveles-de-los-rios-en-paraguay/)
  - 2024: record low of -1.47 m in October. The river only got back to 0 m on 2025-01-07. [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.py/negocios/2025/01/07/el-rio-paraguay-volvio-hoy-al-cero-hidrometrico-en-asuncion/)
  - 2022: back below 0 m by Dec 27. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2022/12/27/nivel-de-los-rios-en-asuncion-nuevamente-se-esta-por-debajo-del-cero-hidrometrico/)
  - 2020: 1.51 m on Dec 22, then falling. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2020/12/28/nivel-del-rio-paraguay-desciende-desde-hace-casi-una-semana/)
  - 2019: 0.74 m on Dec 1, then up to 3.36 m by Dec 29. That shows a single month can swing by more than 2.5 m. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2020/01/02/el-rio-baja-levemente-tras-crecida-paulatina-de-mas-de-dos-metros-en-un-mes/)
  - The search tool also turned up mid-July 2026 readings of about 3.8 m, but those dates are unreliable and conflicting.
- **2026 compared with earlier years:** this year is running well above 2022, 2024 and 2025 for this time of year, because of the October rain-driven rise.
- Typical size of change: this October the river rose 2.3 m in 19 days. Since the peak it has fallen 0.57 m in 10 days.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or Metaculus price for this question. All the markets supplied (Kalshi, Polymarket) are about Paraguayan politics, football or Lake Mead, not this river.
- The DMH Third Hydroclimate Forum (Sep 2026) outlook for Oct to Dec 2026, according to search summaries: levels below average, with expected peak ranges of 2.00 to 2.50 m at Vallemí, 2.30 to 3.00 m at Concepción and 4.00 to 5.00 m at Pilar, and above-normal rain in the Paraguay basin. I could not read the PDF itself to confirm this or find a figure for Asunción. [DMH forum PDF](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/INFORME-FINAL_III-FORO-HIDROCLIMATICO_HOHENAU2026-1.pdf)
- 2026 news coverage also cites a DMH outlook of significant November and December rain that could cause rises. That claim is undated and unverified. [Última Hora](https://www.ultimahora.com/el-rio-paraguay-sigue-creciendo-tras-registrar-la-mayor-bajante-de-su-historia-cual-es-la-proyeccion)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Rain in the lower Paraguay basin and the Chaco, Nov 6 to 30.** A local rainfall event like the one in October could drive another fast rise. Storms on Nov 2 to 4 hit mainly the south and the Bajo Chaco, and Asunción got only light rain.
- **Paraná backwater.** The Paraná is rising after the Nov 4 storms (Encarnación +16 cm) and Pilar is high at 6.38 m. That could slow the fall at Asunción; this is my inference.
- **Upstream contribution.** The Pantanal stations are low and falling slowly (Ladario 0.90 m), so little extra water is coming from upstream.
- **Forecasts.** I did not find an official DMH November forecast for rain or river levels covering the time to resolution.

## Paraguay River at Asunción: research for the December 1, 2026 reading

The river is falling. The official gauge read **2.45 m on Nov 5**, down from a peak of 3.02 m on Oct 26. Over the last five days it fell about 6 cm per day. If that pace held, the level would drop below the question's 2.2 m floor within roughly 4 to 5 days. The best past example (November-December 2022) shows a similar spike draining by more than 3 m in about a month. The main thing that could push the other way is the El Niño outlook for above-normal rain in October-December.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: The DMH station page says it shows the last 60 days but only lists 30 entries (Oct 7 to Nov 5). Latest reading is **2.45 m (Nov 5)**. [DMH](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/nivel-rio/vermas.php?id=2000086218)
- Recent daily series (m): Oct 7 0.73, Oct 9 0.94, Oct 10 1.19, Oct 11 1.55, Oct 12 1.81, Oct 13 2.08, Oct 14 2.29, Oct 15 2.44, Oct 16 2.56, Oct 19 2.73, Oct 22 2.83, Oct 24 2.90, **Oct 26 3.02 (peak)**, Oct 27 3.01, Oct 28 2.99, Oct 29 2.93, Oct 30 2.86, Oct 31 2.76, Nov 1 2.66, Nov 2 2.57, Nov 3 2.57, Nov 4 2.50, Nov 5 2.45. [DMH](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/nivel-rio/vermas.php?id=2000086218)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The river has been falling steadily for 10 days, by about 0.57 m since the peak. It paused on Nov 2-3 and then kept falling.
- 2026-11-02: News reports said the rain so far had not been enough to stop the fall at Asunción. [Crónica](https://www.cronica.com.py/2026/11/02/el-rio-paraguay-sigue-bajando-y-ya-esta-en-257-metros-en-asuncion/); [RDN](https://www.rdn.com.py/2026/11/02/rio-paraguay-baja-otros-nueve-centimetros-en-asuncion)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: The DMH issued severe storm alerts for the southern departments (Itapúa, Misiones). Encarnación got 102.5 mm in one day. This area mostly drains to the Paraná, not the Paraguay above Asunción. [Primera Edición](https://www.primeraedicion.com.ar/nota/101157645/tormentas-en-paraguay-encarnacion-registro-mas-de-100-milimetros-de-lluvia-y-persiste-el-alerta/)
- 2026-11-02: Reading of 2.57 m. A Sunday storm hit the Bajo Chaco region but did not raise the river. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/clima/2026/11/02/el-rio-paraguay-baja-otros-nueve-centimetros-en-la-bahia-de-asuncion/)
- 2026-10-19: Reading of 2.74 m. The alert level is 4.50 m. The Asunción municipality declared an emergency, with about 3,300 riverside families at risk if the river reached 3.5 m. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2026/10/19/el-rio-paraguay-casi-llega-a-los-tres-metros-en-la-bahia-de-asuncion/)
- 2026-10-18: The Paraná River was on red alert at Ciudad del Este, with more than 1,200 people evacuated. [PAHO](https://www.paho.org/en/natural-hazards-monitoring/natural-hazards-monitoring-19-october-2026)
- 2026-10-13: Heavy rain in early October drove the rise, from 0.43 m at the end of September to 1.81 m on Oct 12. The article links it to El Niño. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/clima/2026/10/13/nivel-del-rio-paraguay-en-la-bahia-de-asuncion-aumento-mas-de-un-metro-en-15-dias/)
- 2026-09-30: Reading of 0.49 m, described as "critical". The historical average for that date is about 2 m. The 2026 peak so far was 3.31 m in mid-May. [ABC](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2026/09/30/nivel-de-rios-mientras-el-parana-sube-el-paraguay-continua-bajo/)

### 4. Base rates
- The October rise was fast and driven by local rain (about 2.3 m in about 19 days). That points to quick runoff rather than a slow flood wave from upstream, which suggests a fast drop afterward.
- **Closest past example, 2022:** a peak of 3.59 m on Nov 23, about 2.5 m in early December, about 0.5 m on Dec 14, and -0.01 m on Dec 27. That is a fall of more than 3 m in about a month. [ABC 2022](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2022/12/27/nivel-de-los-rios-en-asuncion-nuevamente-se-esta-por-debajo-del-cero-hidrometrico/)
- **2024-25:** a record low of about -1.71 m on Nov 2, 2024 (other sources say -1.47). Rain lifted it to 0.77 m by Dec 23, then it fell about 4 cm per day to -0.15 m by Jan 13, 2025. [Paraguay Fluvial](https://paraguayfluvial.com/rio-paraguay-desciende-92-cm-en-19-dias-alcanzando-015-m-en-asuncion/)
- **2021:** a record low of -0.75 m in October. **2020:** about 0.84 m on Dec 14. [ABC 2020](https://www.abc.com.py/nacionales/2020/12/14/nivel-del-rio-paraguay-sube-nuevamente-y-queda-a-16-cm-del-metro-de-altura/)
- **Seasonal comparison (early Nov to Dec 1):** I could not find exact Dec 1 values for 2023 or 2025. Most recent years (2020, 2021, 2024) had levels at or below about 1 m in late November and early December. Only 2022 was spiking. On the current reading, 2026 is running well above most recent years but came from a very low September.
- **Recent pace:** -0.31 m over Oct 31 to Nov 5 (about 6 cm per day), and -0.57 m in 10 days since the peak.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast for this question. The Kalshi and Polymarket markets provided (Paraguayan elections, Lake Mead, football) are unrelated.
- No DMH river-level forecast for Asunción in November or December was found. A March 2026 outlook forum gave Fuerte Olimpo (far upstream) a November-January range of 2.5 to 3.5 m. This was only a search-result snippet; I did not open the document. [comip PDF](https://comip.org.ar/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DMH-DINAC-Perspectivas-Hidroclimaticas-A-M-J-2026.pdf)

### 6. Upcoming events before Dec 1
- **September outlook (III Foro Hidroclimático, DMH):** above-normal rain expected in the Región Oriental and southeastern Chaco for October-December. It puts a 75% chance on an El Niño event of historic magnitude in that quarter. Snippets also mention a probability above 90% that Paraguay River flows stay above normal, but that text was incomplete. I could not read the PDF itself; these claims come from search snippets. [DMH PDF](https://www.meteorologia.gov.py/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/INFORME-FINAL_III-FORO-HIDROCLIMATICO_HOHENAU2026-1.pdf)
- 2026-09-02: The DMH said El Niño was showing its first signs and could last into 2027. [La Nación](https://www.lanacion.com.py/pais/2026/09/02/fenomeno-el-nino-paraguay-reporta-primeras-senales-y-se-extenderia-hasta-el-2027/)
- **Things that could move the level:**
  - Heavy rain over the lower basin near Asunción or the eastern region, which caused the October spike. Repeated storm systems are forecast.
  - Water held back by a high Paraná. This is my inference and unverified.
  - If neither happens, the drop continues. The 2022 and 2024-25 recessions ran about 4 to 10+ cm per day.
- I found no short-range official river forecast covering the period to Dec 1.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 25 days. The question resolves on the DMH reading for December 1, 2026.

(b) Latest known value: 2.45 m at Asunción on 2026-11-05, down 5 cm on the day.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 2.45 m.

(d) If the current trend continued:
- At a constant 5 to 7 cm/day, the river would reach roughly 0.7 to 1.2 m by December 1.
- The daily drops are shrinking, though (-10, -10, -9, 0, -7, -5 cm). If the rate of fall halves roughly every week, the remaining decline is about 0.4 to 0.6 m, giving about 1.8 to 2.0 m.
- Upstream, Concepción (1.96 m) is falling about 2 cm/day, so there is still slow drainage underneath.
- The high and rising Paraná (Pilar at 6.38 m) likely backs water up the Paraguay and slows the fall. This is inference, not a sourced claim.

(e) Historical variation: the river can move 2 m or more in a month. It rose 2.3 m in 19 days this October, and in December 2019 it went from 0.74 to 3.36 m within one month. Typical November behaviour is a slow fall or flat levels, with a rain-driven rise possible.

(f) Experts and markets:
- There is no market on this question.
- The DMH outlook for October to December reportedly calls for above-normal rain but below-average levels, and some coverage mentions possible rises in November and December. Neither claim is verified.
- The question creator's range of 2.2 to 4.2 m suggests they expected levels to stay near current values, but it was likely set when the river was near its peak.

(g) Scenarios:
- Low: a dry November across the Chaco and lower basin, with the Paraná backwater easing, gives a steady recession of 4 to 5 cm/day to about 1.1 m.
- High: repeated heavy storms over the lower basin, like those in October, plus a rising Paraná, give another rise to 3 to 3.5 m or more.

My median is about 1.9 m, with a right skew for rain risk.

(b) **Latest known value:** 2.45 m on 2026-11-05 at the DMH Asunción station, down 5 cm that day.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 2.45 m.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The daily falls are getting smaller: -10, -10, -9, 0, -7, -5 cm. Keeping 5 cm/day for 26 days would give about 1.15 m. That is unlikely, because recessions slow down as they go on. If the fall eases to an average of 2.5 to 3.5 cm/day, the level would be about 1.55 to 1.8 m.
- Upstream stations are only falling slowly (Concepción -2 cm/day).
- The Paraná is high and rising, which probably backs water up the Paraguay and slows the fall at Asunción.

(e) **Historical variation:** One month can move the level by more than 2.5 m. In December 2019 it went from 0.74 to 3.36 m, and this October it rose 2.3 m in 19 days. In a dry month the recession usually takes off 0.5 to 1.2 m.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- There is no market on this question.
- The DMH forum outlook calls for below-average levels but above-normal rain in Oct to Dec.
- Unverified reports mention significant November and December rain that could cause rises.
- The question creator's range is 2.2 to 4.2 m. That range seems anchored on the current level and does not account for the recession.
